policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'captivity' does not distinguish the qere שְׁבוּתְכֶם from the ketiv שביתכם, and the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering, so it cannot decide the reading; retain the qere base fallback.

ASV 'an astonishment' does not distinguish the qere לְזַעֲוָה from the ketiv לזועה, and the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering, so it cannot decide the reading; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV 'I am he that knoweth' is compatible with both the qere הַיּוֹדֵעַ and the ketiv הו ידע, and no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them; retain the qere base fallback.
